title: Human Rights
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Keep Childline 116 on the board. A learner who discloses harm is followed up privately under the school's safeguarding policy.

skills.key_step: The child names basic human rights and tells a right from a want.

floor.question: Name one right of a child.

representations: a story of a child denied a right
steps: Ask: does every person need it to live with dignity?
If yes, it is a right.
If not, it is a want.
contexts: a family with a name and nationality for each child
a learner wanting a new phone

board.do: Write education, a toy, health care, sweets.

misconceptions.repair: Sort cards into needs that protect life and dignity and things that are nice to have.

misconceptions.ask: Who has the right to education?
misconceptions.repair: Read the children's rights list aloud.

misconceptions.ask: Does a child lose the right to education for bad behaviour?
misconceptions.repair: Sort: break time football (privilege) and education (right).

misconceptions.ask: Do rich and poor children have the same rights?
misconceptions.repair: Separate things a family can buy from rights the law gives everyone.

checks.question: Give two basic human rights.
checks.answer: any two of: life, education, health care, a name and nationality, protection, play and rest

checks.question: Is a mobile phone a basic human right?

skills.key_step: The child pairs a right with its responsibility, says rights protect everyone, and names who helps when rights are denied.

floor.question: Name one basic human right.
floor.answer: any right such as health care

steps: Name the duty that goes with it.
Say who to tell if a right is denied.
contexts: a learner taking turns to speak in class
a girl kept from school to work
a friend who is being hurt at home

board.do: Draw a balance: right on one side, duty on the other.
Point at "the right to be safe".

misconceptions.ask: Eve says she has a right to play loud music at night. What is missing?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whose rights are touched when the music is loud.

listen_for: Keep quiet because it is a family matter
misconceptions.ask: A child is beaten badly at home. What should another child do?
misconceptions.repair: Practise telling a teacher and call Childline 116.

misconceptions.ask: Which responsibility goes with the right to education?
misconceptions.repair: Pair each right with the duty that protects it for you and others.

misconceptions.ask: Your right to speak means you should...
misconceptions.repair: Run a talk where only one learner may speak, then a fair turn-taking talk.

checks.question: Which responsibility goes with the right to a clean environment?
A child is kept from school to work. Who can help?
checks.answer: a teacher, a trusted adult, the children's office or Childline 116
